segments.he: עַל יְדֵי זִכְרוֹן עוֹלָם הַבָּא יַעֲסֹק בְּהִתְבּוֹדְדוּת
segments.en: But afterward, when the evil inclination has already overpowered him, Heaven forbid, and tripped him up in whatever it tripped him — afterward he must put aside the shame from his face and make bold before Hashem, to say: "Even though I have done what I have done, and I am ashamed and mortified to lift my face to You — even so, I make bold before You and beseech You to draw me close to You even now." And even if it happened this way many times, Heaven forbid, one must never collapse in resolve — only to strengthen and begin anew each time, as long as one's soul is within him. And this is the essence of holy boldness — not to weaken in resolve because of what has passed, but to forget each time everything that has gone before and to begin anew each time.

segments.he: זֶה רוֹאִין בְּחוּשׁ שֶׁעִקַּר הִתְגָּרוּת הָרַע עַיִן שֶׁהוּא כְּלַל כָּל הַחוֹלְקִים וְהַמִּתְנַגְּדִים עַל הָאֱמֶת. הֵן מֵהָעַכּוּ"ם. הֵן מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל בְּאֵיזֶה בְּחִינָה שֶׁהִיא. עִקַּר הִתְגָּרוּתָם הוּא עַל בְּחִינַת הַזִכָּרוֹן בִּפְרָטִיּוּת. דְּהַיְנוּ מַה שֶּׁצַּדִּיקֵי אֱמֶת מוֹרִים אוֹתָנוּ דְּרָכִים יְשָׁרִים אֲמִתִּיִּים עַל פִּי הַתּוֹרָה הַקְּדוֹשָׁה אֵיךְ לְהַמְשִׁיךְ עָלֵינוּ הַזִכָּרוֹן הַזֶּה בִּפְרָטִיּוּת. עַל זֶה הֵם מִתְגָּרִים וְחוֹלְקִים וְאוֹמְרִים שֶׁלּא זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ רַק רוֹצִים שֶׁהַכּל יֵלְכוּ בְּדַרְכָּם לְבַלּוֹת הַיָּמִים בְּלֵיצָנוּת וּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים וְלִרְדּף אַחַר הַמָּמוֹן תָּמִיד וְכַיּוֹצֵא בָּזֶה וּמַלְבִּישִׁים הַשֶּׁקֶר בְּאֵיזֶה אֱמֶת כְּאִלּוּ כַּוָּנָתָם לַשָּׁמַיִם...
segments.en: This is the aspect of Torah and prayer. For the totality of Torah is the aspect of thought and daas, the aspect of Moshe — this is the aspect of Torah She'biksav. And prayer is the aspect of bringing one to action — the aspect of speech, the aspect of Torah She'b'al Peh. For the very essence of one's overcoming the evil inclination and the blood and standing firm against all obstacles until one comes to action — this is through prayer, as is understood from the words of Rabbainu of blessed memory many times, that the essence of one's overcoming to merit all matters in holiness is through prayer, which is the aspect of Dovid, the aspect of "and I am prayer" [Tehillim 109:4] — which is the aspect of the entire Book of Tehillim that he composed, which is five books corresponding to the Five Books of the Torah. That is, his entire effort and overcoming, in fighting the wars of Hashem and in establishing many prayers written in the Book of Tehillim, was in order to bring all the commandments to the level of action — to merit to fulfill the Torah that Moshe Rabbainu commanded us. As is understood from the Torah teaching Ays Lanu Beira [Likutay Moharan 31], that the primary formation of the Torah's letters for good comes through prayer — through speaking one's longing aloud with the mouth.

segments.he: אֲבָל מִי שֶׁיָּשִׂים אֶל לִבּוֹ הֵיטֵב זִכְרוֹן עוֹלָם הַבָּא בֶּאֱמֶת לַאֲמִתּוֹ.
segments.en: One who wishes to have compassion on his own soul, so as not to lose his world, Heaven forbid, must search and investigate greatly after truth in order to return to Hashem in truth. For perhaps his mind misleads him in some way, because he has not merited to form the light properly, since his vessels are incomplete due to the flaw of the bris — as discussed above. And the primary remedy for all this is "let us lift our hearts to our palms, to G-d in the heavens" [Eichah 3:41] — which is the aspect of crying out and prayer and conversation and hisbodidus in seclusion with one's Maker, for one must cry out greatly to Hashem with complete self-sacrifice until it is as if the soul nearly departs — as our Rabbis of blessed memory said: A person's prayer is not heard unless he places his soul in his palm, and they derived this from this very verse.

segments.he: בְּוַדַּאי יָבִין גַּם בִּפְרָטִיּוּת אֵיזֶהוּ דֶּרֶךְ יְשָׁרָה לָלֶכֶת בּוֹ. אִם לְבַלּוֹת יָמָיו עַל מַה שֶּׁהֵם מְבַלִּים רַחֲמָנָא לִצְלָן. אִם לְבַלּוֹת יָמָיו עַל הִתְבּוֹדְדוּת וְתוֹרָה וּתְפִלָּה וּצְעָקָה לַה' יִתְבָּרַךְ וְכוּ' כַּאֲשֶׁר הוֹרוּ אוֹתָנוּ צַדִּיקֵי אֱמֶת. (הִלְכוֹת בִּרְכוֹת הָרְאִיָּה הֲלָכָה ה אוֹת ד):
segments.en: For the primary rectification of the bris is through much crying out to Hashem — one must cry out at least seventy kolin [voices/cries]. And within these seventy cries are included innumerable voices and outcries and prayers and supplications, for one must pray about this throughout all the days of one's life. The seventy cries correspond to the seventy facets of the Torah which every person in Yisrael must merit. And each person can understand within himself how far he still is from even one facet of the holy Torah, and all the more so from all of them. Therefore, even if one has not committed many transgressions, and even if one has already cried out greatly to Hashem and performed many commandments and studied much Torah — even so, since one sees that one has not yet attained even one part in a thousand or ten-thousand of even one facet of the Torah, how very much must one still cry out to Hashem throughout all the days of one's life.
